chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Isa ibn Bashir, from Abu Hamza, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When the death of my father, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), approached, he pressed me to his chest and said: 'O my son! I bequeath to you what my father bequeathed to me when death approached him, and what he mentioned that his father bequeathed to him: O my son! Be patient with the truth, even if it is bitter.'

key_terms.أُوصِيكَ: I bequeath to you / I advise you
key_terms.ضَمَّنِي إِلَى صَدْرِهِ: Pressed me to his chest (a gesture of affection and emphasis)

ai.seo_question: What was the final advice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn to his son regarding patience and truth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the transmission of spiritual authority (tawsiyah) within the Ahl al-Bayt, where Imam Muhammad al-Baqir receives the final counsel of his father, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn. The instruction to 'be patient with the truth even if it is bitter' underscores the Shia concept of sabr not merely as passive endurance, but as active, steadfast adherence to divine reality amidst hardship. This legacy connects the Imams' personal trials to the broader theological necessity of maintaining fidelity to Haqq (Truth) despite its difficulties.
